Observed-but-unowned row as furnace_observe leaves it (cd pin-ce180d82 && env -u CLAUDECODE ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run --config ../probes/observe/vitest.probe.config.mts c-control -> probes/observe/out/C3-no-ownership.json): 'No native-confirmed lifecycle ownership of the target.' Wiring absence by code-read: grep -rn 'applyDetachedReading\|projectDetachedReading' src -> definitions only (src/workbench/detached-observer.ts:109, :152); src/index.ts:2901-2902 (refresh only, no relate); grep -rn 'abortController.abort()' src -> src/index.ts:1254 (session_shutdown) and src/ui/workflow-menu.ts:275 only. The repo says so itself: test/workbench-detached-control-live.test.ts:13-14 ('declared UNREALISED citing wb-79k.3 (HELD): nothing in src ingests detached readings'), test/workbench-furnace-control-live.test.ts:13-18 ('STRICT-READING LIMIT ... decideControl would deny cross-scope or no-confirmed-ownership'). Docs still list them as legs: docs/workbench/11-designer-and-operator.md:14. Graded SUPPORTED because no real furnace Run or detached host was admitted here; the forge leg IS reachable (probes/observe/out/D1-forge-readback.json ownershipConfirmationRef from the server's step frame) and the claude-agent-sdk interrupt leg is admitted through the booted tools in the default-gate fixture suite (test/workbench-pi-claude-control.test.ts 11/11, probes/observe/out/L-pi-claude-control.log).
cost: Any agent that launches a detached workflow or observes a Furnace Run and then needs to stop it, and any agent that wants to cancel its own embedded workflow: every attempt ends in a refusal with no next step; the operator must use /agents -> Workflows.
cureHint: Wire applyDetachedReading on workflow_detached launch/inspect and workflow_execute detached; relate the Run->Attempt ownership the FurnaceObserver already reads; add an owned 'cancel' for pi-workflow tasks (the host owns the AbortController). Until then, say in the description which providers are admissible.

claim: The repo's own reply-size bench for this tool prints nothing until it finishes — 310 s on this host — and Node warns on every run that dist/*.js is reparsed as ES module because package.json declares no module type.

Reparsing as ES module ... This incurs a performance overhead.' Host load average was 139-180 during the run (uptime), so the duration is an upper bound for a loaded host, not a quiet-host figure.
cost: Anyone running the W21 receipt by hand or under a timeout: a run that looks hung, and a stderr warning on every dist-backed QA script.
cureHint: Emit a progress line per series on stderr (12 series) and state the expected duration in the header; set the module type for dist (or emit .mjs) so Node does not reparse.
